top_news.title: Zardari says oppn should engage with Centre on counterterrorism to lift emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
top_news.summary: In a move underscoring the deep political fracturing and expanding security footprint in Pakistan, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday signalled that the federal government could lift emergency rule and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) if the opposition engages with Islamabad on an anti-terrorism plan, according to Dawn. The statements come amid growing concerns over the Rawalpindi establishment leveraging security pretexts to systematically dismantle political opposition and consolidate power, following the federal government's takeover and imposition of emergency rule in former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) stronghold in KP. According to Dawn, Bhutto-Zardari, while speaking to the media in Karachi while visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the 2007 Karsaz bombing, defended the federal takeover in KP while placing the onus squarely on the opposition. "If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor's rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism," Bilawal said, as reported by Dawn. He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and "we agree on a plan" to do so, the emergency and governor's rule in KP could end. The takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, executed by the federal government citing the provincial administration's alleged "deliberate disengagement" from anti-terror efforts, followed a massive mobilisation drive and long march led by the PTI to demand the immediate release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan. Calling out the provincial leadership, the PPP chief aimed sharp criticism at former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. "If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them," Bilawal said, according to Dawn. "That is why we supported the government's decision to impose governor's rule in KP." He stressed that his party would "join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists". Reflecting on the escalating cross-border violence and militant attacks across Pakistan, Bilawal conceded that the security situation was deteriorating drastically. In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where "terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar". He added that the country had now once again reached the point where "some forces want to take down Pakistan's flag in Swat" and there was an ongoing national fight against terrorism targeting security personnel, law enforcement, and civilians alike. However, he claimed that in KP, where the highest frequency of attacks is concentrated, the chief minister had pledged not to face the terrorists. top_news.title: Trump claims
top_news.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (local time) claimed that negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict were making "great progress", while defending his administration's diplomatic approach towards Moscow and accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of failing to secure a better deal two years ago. In a post on Truth Social, Trump described his strategy to strike a deal between the warring nations as a simple one which he said includes ensuring that Russia is not, "foolishly", driven away from the bargaining table. Trump said that the diplomatic process is making great strides, touting that he can sign the document that involves ongoing hostage negotiations "anytime that I want." "My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made, and that includes current hostage negotiations! Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump wrote. Furthermore, Trump addressed claims of Russia helping Iran and stated that Moscow's efforts are "very little" in regard to its capabilities, adding that he "wants to keep it that way." "Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way," he added. The US President subsequently criticised Zelenskyy over Ukrainian attacks targeting Russian diesel refineries, stating that these are hurting the global energy markets, while commending Russia for selling diesel "at a low price" after Moscow agreed to supply more than 3,00,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, followed by another 5,00,000 tonnes during November and 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter as part of the deal with the US. "Lastly, Zelenskyy is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States. Farmers, ranchers, and businesses of all kinds are suffering greatly from this, but Russia is, nevertheless, sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World," he added. Trump further asserted that his Ukrainian counterpart does not want to end the ongoing conflict to continue availing financial benefits from Europe and the US, such as in the previous Joe Biden-led administration. The US President painted Zelenskyy as responsible for the deterioration of his country amid the conflict, accusing him of not striking a better deal "two years ago." "Zelenskyy doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did. He could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now. His country is in shambles, a large portion of his land is lost, his oceans and seas are gone, and his male population is low, wounded, and/or dead," Trump asserted, while reiterating that "I WANT THIS WAR END!" Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Moscow has launched dozens of strikes targeting the nation's critical infrastructure over the past week, despite a diplomatic announcement regarding a temporary halt. "Since the American President announced the energy ceasefire a week ago, Russia has deliberately attacked Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors 76 times," he wrote on X, noting that recent bombardments impacted electrical installations across the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi and Odesa regions. Zelenskyy also warned that Washington's decision to ease certain sanctions against Russia could encourage further aggression by Moscow. He expressed concern that additional sanctions relief could follow, arguing that such measures would not help end hostilities. An executive order signed by the US leader reversed crucial Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs that were originally set to take effect under the newly enacted Graham Act. Administration officials maintained that the temporary relief served national security priorities. The legislative framework was designed to ramp up economic pressure on Moscow following the military escalation in 2022. Responding to the policy shift, Zelenskyy argued that easing restrictions would reinforce Moscow's willingness to continue military operations rather than encourage negotiations. "It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskyy. "This certainly does not stop the war." (ANI)

articles.title: Zardari says oppn should engage with Centre on counterterrorism to lift emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
articles.summary: In a move underscoring the deep political fracturing and expanding security footprint in Pakistan, Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday signalled that the federal government could lift emergency rule and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) if the opposition engages with Islamabad on an anti-terrorism plan, according to Dawn. The statements come amid growing concerns over the Rawalpindi establishment leveraging security pretexts to systematically dismantle political opposition and consolidate power, following the federal government's takeover and imposition of emergency rule in former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan-led Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) stronghold in KP. According to Dawn, Bhutto-Zardari, while speaking to the media in Karachi while visiting the Karsaz Monument on the 19th anniversary of the 2007 Karsaz bombing, defended the federal takeover in KP while placing the onus squarely on the opposition. "If they really want to fight terrorists, and if they want that emergency and governor's rule in KP to end, they should engage with the federal government and politicians and discuss a united policy regarding the fight against terrorism," Bilawal said, as reported by Dawn. He added that if the opposition was ready to fight terrorism and "we agree on a plan" to do so, the emergency and governor's rule in KP could end. The takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, executed by the federal government citing the provincial administration's alleged "deliberate disengagement" from anti-terror efforts, followed a massive mobilisation drive and long march led by the PTI to demand the immediate release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan. Calling out the provincial leadership, the PPP chief aimed sharp criticism at former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. "If the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister is a coward, if he is not ready to defend his homeland, if he is not ready to fight those terrorists, then the PPP is ready to fight them," Bilawal said, according to Dawn. "That is why we supported the government's decision to impose governor's rule in KP." He stressed that his party would "join forces with everyone to fight these terrorists". Reflecting on the escalating cross-border violence and militant attacks across Pakistan, Bilawal conceded that the security situation was deteriorating drastically. In his media talk, the Bhutto scion said the country had reached a point where "terrorist attacks are taking place from Khyber to Khuzdar". He added that the country had now once again reached the point where "some forces want to take down Pakistan's flag in Swat" and there was an ongoing national fight against terrorism targeting security personnel, law enforcement, and civilians alike. However, he claimed that in KP, where the highest frequency of attacks is concentrated, the chief minister had pledged not to face the terrorists. Addressing Pakistan's deep-seated financial instability, which continues to worsen under heavy militarisation and political deadlock, Bilawal highlighted the country's dire situation, Dawn reported. Answering questions, he stated that Pakistan was facing a "historic economic crisis". "It appears that the situation will worsen. Our priority is to address this economic crisis, and to do that, we will have to fight terrorism as well," he added. Emphasising the necessity of political consensus, Bilawal noted that efforts should also be made to improve the democratic and electoral system in Pakistan. His remarks come as Pakistan's establishment has plunged further into authoritarian descent by enforcing a state of emergency and Governor's Rule across the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, resulting in the practical suspension of the regional administration headed by imprisoned ex-premier Imran Khan's political outfit, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. The emergency directive was formally brought into effect on Sunday, October 11, 2026, invoking Articles 232 and 234 of the national charter. Terrorism within Pakistan is fundamentally homegrown, stemming from a deliberate policy implemented by the nation for more than five decades in its pursuit of strategic depth. As former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton famously remarked, one cannot rear snakes in a backyard and expect them to bite only neighbours, as they will eventually turn on their keepers. Rather than learning from this outcome, Pakistan began differentiating between acceptable and unacceptable terrorist factions. The state has also flip-flopped in its approach toward elements hostile to it. During General Bajwa's tenure, Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) cadres were relocated to parts of the erstwhile Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK). Facing a failure to manage the security situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, authorities have responded by imposing a state of emergency and Governor's Rule overnight. Having previously incarcerated a former Prime Minister and eroded judicial independence through constitutional amendments, the administration has now deprived its principal opposition party of its last remaining provincial government, marking another blow to elected governance amidst ongoing democratic backsliding. (ANI)

articles.title: Trump claims
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday (local time) claimed that negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict were making "great progress", while defending his administration's diplomatic approach towards Moscow and accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of failing to secure a better deal two years ago. In a post on Truth Social, Trump described his strategy to strike a deal between the warring nations as a simple one which he said includes ensuring that Russia is not, "foolishly", driven away from the bargaining table. Trump said that the diplomatic process is making great strides, touting that he can sign the document that involves ongoing hostage negotiations "anytime that I want." "My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made, and that includes current hostage negotiations! Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump wrote. Furthermore, Trump addressed claims of Russia helping Iran and stated that Moscow's efforts are "very little" in regard to its capabilities, adding that he "wants to keep it that way." "Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way, and will, unless stupid people get in the way," he added. The US President subsequently criticised Zelenskyy over Ukrainian attacks targeting Russian diesel refineries, stating that these are hurting the global energy markets, while commending Russia for selling diesel "at a low price" after Moscow agreed to supply more than 3,00,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, followed by another 5,00,000 tonnes during November and 1 million tonnes immediately thereafter as part of the deal with the US. "Lastly, Zelenskyy is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States. Farmers, ranchers, and businesses of all kinds are suffering greatly from this, but Russia is, nevertheless, sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World," he added. Trump further asserted that his Ukrainian counterpart does not want to end the ongoing conflict to continue availing financial benefits from Europe and the US, such as in the previous Joe Biden-led administration. The US President painted Zelenskyy as responsible for the deterioration of his country amid the conflict, accusing him of not striking a better deal "two years ago." "Zelenskyy doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did. He could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now. His country is in shambles, a large portion of his land is lost, his oceans and seas are gone, and his male population is low, wounded, and/or dead," Trump asserted, while reiterating that "I WANT THIS WAR END!" Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Moscow has launched dozens of strikes targeting the nation's critical infrastructure over the past week, despite a diplomatic announcement regarding a temporary halt. "Since the American President announced the energy ceasefire a week ago, Russia has deliberately attacked Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors 76 times," he wrote on X, noting that recent bombardments impacted electrical installations across the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi and Odesa regions. Zelenskyy also warned that Washington's decision to ease certain sanctions against Russia could encourage further aggression by Moscow. He expressed concern that additional sanctions relief could follow, arguing that such measures would not help end hostilities. An executive order signed by the US leader reversed crucial Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs that were originally set to take effect under the newly enacted Graham Act. Administration officials maintained that the temporary relief served national security priorities. The legislative framework was designed to ramp up economic pressure on Moscow following the military escalation in 2022. Responding to the policy shift, Zelenskyy argued that easing restrictions would reinforce Moscow's willingness to continue military operations rather than encourage negotiations. "It only fuels their satisfaction and their desire to keep killing people," wrote Zelenskyy. "This certainly does not stop the war." (ANI)

articles.title: US issues Saudi Arabia travel alert; warns citizens against filming strike sites amid escalating tensions
articles.summary: The US Embassy and Consulates in Saudi Arabia on Sunday (local time) issued a heightened security alert warning American citizens of ongoing missile and drone attacks targeting major airports across the Kingdom. The security warning follows recent aerial strikes that forced operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh to remain suspended. In response, Washington has placed strict travel restrictions on its diplomatic personnel and cautioned foreign visitors that capturing footage of missile impact sites carries severe legal consequences. Due to the elevated threat to commercial aviation, the US mission has restricted travel for all American government staff stationed in Saudi Arabia. "U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom," the official embassy stated. Warning travellers of widespread flight disruptions and potential airspace closures across major hubs, the embassy urged extreme caution. "Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport," the statement read. With the capital's main airport shut down, the embassy advised citizens to monitor local emergency alerts and consider travelling over land, as highway routes and border crossings remain open. "U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. Private car, train, and bus options may provide alternatives to air travel to or from Saudi Arabia... All land border crossings, including the King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain, remain operational. All highways and roads in and around Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dhahran remain operational," it noted. "International airports in neighboring countries of Bahrain (BAH), Jordan (AMM), Oman (MCT), Qatar (DOH), and the United Arab Emirates (AUH, DXB, SHJ) remain operational," the statement added. "Please confirm status directly with airports." Furthermore, the US Embassy reminded American citizens that Saudi authorities strictly enforce laws prohibiting any public filming or distribution of photos showing counter-missile defence operations and strike locations. "Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior continues to warn that 'filming, publishing, or sharing information related to counter-missiles and drones, and their impact sites, exposes you to legal liability,'" the embassy warned."U.S. citizens have been detained for not adhering to these regulations, including taking photos of government buildings, airports, and impact sites.
